articles.title: India's First Book on GCC Governance Launched by Telangana IT & Legislative Affairs ...
articles.content: ADVERTISEMENT HYDERABAD, TELANGANA: In a landmark moment for India’s Global Capability Center (GCC) industry, GCC Governance: Mastering Law, Risk, and Leadership in Global Capability Centers — billed as the first book of its kind in India — was officially launched by D. Sridhar Babu, IT & Legislative Affairs Minister, Government of Telangana . The book is authored by Dr. Kurella Venkata Chakrapani , a senior finance, tax, and governance leader with over two decades of experience building, scaling, and transforming global enterprises, and is published by Gurucool Publishing . The launch marks a significant milestone for a publication focused squarely on the governance challenges and opportunities shaping India’s booming GCC sector — a segment that has evolved from a cost-efficient back-office model into a strategic engine of innovation, digital transformation, and global value creation. ADVERTISEMENT A Systems-Led Approach to a Complex Challenge Modern GCCs operate across multiple jurisdictions, regulatory frameworks, business functions, and stakeholder groups, where decisions on taxation, labour law, contracts, data, intellectual property, compliance, and ESG can no longer be treated as isolated issues. GCC Governance reframes governance as a systems-led discipline in which individual decisions ripple across organizational structures, risk profiles, and business outcomes. Rather than positioning governance as a mere compliance requirement, Dr. Chakrapani presents it as a strategic capability — one that supports agility, accountability, resilience, and long-term enterprise growth. The book argues that as GCCs scale, traditional, fragmented compliance models are no longer sufficient, and calls for frameworks that integrate legal understanding, financial insight, risk management, and leadership judgment into a single, cohesive approach. Key Areas Covered The book explores the critical domains shaping the operation and growth of global capability centers, including: Regulatory structuring Taxation Labour laws Data governance Intellectual property Contracting Risk management Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) responsibilities By connecting these disciplines, the book equips leaders to identify risks earlier, strengthen accountability, and build governance structures capable of adapting to changing regulatory and business conditions — positioning governance not as a control function, but as a genuine strategic advantage. About the Author Dr. Kurella Venkata Chakrapani is a senior finance, tax, and governance leader with more than two decades of experience building, scaling, and transforming global enterprises. He has led complex global assignments spanning operational excellence, strategic service delivery, regulatory alignment, and governance design. As a board member, thought leader, and speaker, he works with organizations to navigate complexity through clarity of decisions and sustainable governance frameworks, and continues to shape the evolving role of GCCs in the global business landscape. Who Should Read This Book GCC Governance is written for GCC leaders, finance and tax professionals, legal and compliance experts, board members, risk managers, consultants, and business executives, as well as aspiring GCC leaders seeking to understand the evolving relationship between governance, risk, law, leadership, and enterprise transformation. articles.title: India's First 21 CuM Electric Shovel Commissioned in Chhattisgarh by SECL - Indian PSU
articles.content: India’s first 21 CuM capacity electro-hydraulic face shovel has been commissioned at SECL’s Gevra Mega Project in Korba district, Chhattisgarh. SECL Chairman-cum-Managing Director Harish Duhan inaugurated the state-of-the-art machine today. Gevra is Asia’s largest coal mine. The advanced shovel is expected to further enhance coal production capacity at Gevra while strengthening modern, safe and high-efficiency mining operations. SECL Director (Technical, Planning & Projects) Ramesh Chandra Mahapatra was also present on the occasion. The 21 CuM electro-hydraulic face shovel is equipped with advanced safety and operator-centric features, including a 360-degree camera, Operator Fatigue Monitoring System, air-suspension seat, adjustable joysticks, hydraulic access stairs, gas-based fire suppression system and a FOPS-compliant safety cabin. The machine has also been integrated with SECL’s Fleet Management System (FMS), enabling real-time monitoring of its performance and operational efficiency. With an annual production capacity of approximately 5.31 million cubic metres, the shovel is expected to further strengthen productivity, safety and operational efficiency at the Gevra Mega Project. AGM Sanjay Mishra, along with other senior officers and employees of the Gevra Project, was present during the commissioning ceremony. Indian PSU Desk August 22, 2026 15 1 minute read

The Conclave witnessed insightful discussions and deliberations on Green Hydrogen, clean energy transition, sustainable port development and emerging green technologies, fostering global collaboration and exchange of ideas towards accelerating India’s green maritime ambitions. As part of the Kandla Green Hydrogen Conclave 2026, the GH2 delegation visited India’s first Make-in-India 1-MW Green Hydrogen Plant, at Kandla. articles.title: CAREERIPA Launches One of India's First Science-Backed, AI -Powered Career ...
articles.content: ADVERTISEMENT Structured assessments across Interest, Personality and Ability are fused by an AI mapping engine into ranked, explainable career recommendations — moving people from career confusion to career clarity. BENGALURU: CareerIPA Innovation Pvt Ltd today announced the launch of CareerIPA ( careeripa.com ), a science-backed, AI-powered career guidance platform built to help students, graduates, working professionals, parents, counsellors, schools, colleges, universities and corporates make more informed, personalised career decisions. The platform unifies three validated assessment models — Interest, Personality and Ability (IPA) — and uses a proprietary AI engine to convert the results into a ranked, fully explained career shortlist. ADVERTISEMENT The Problem Every year, millions of students and professionals in India — and worldwide — choose a stream, a degree, or a next career move based on academic marks, family pressure, peer influence or a single one-dimensional aptitude test, rather than structured, evidence-based guidance. According to CareerIPA, this produces a predictable and costly chain reaction: students enrol in wrong-fit courses, graduates emerge disengaged and under-skilled, professionals remain stuck in careers they never truly chose, and parents, institutions and employers are left to manage the fallout without dependable tools to prevent it. This cycle underscores the need for a decision-making framework grounded in psychometric evidence, real-time career-demand data and structured stakeholder support — precisely the gap CareerIPA has been built to close. The Solution: One Framework, Three Sciences, One Certain Answer CareerIPA replaces guesswork with a single online assessment journey built on three complementary, scientifically grounded models — the first platform to score all three signals simultaneously: what drives you, who you are, and what you can master. Derived RIASEC Model (DRM) — Interest : An evolution of Holland’s globally established RIASEC theory, recalibrated for today’s career landscape to reveal what genuinely drives a person. Behavioural Dynamics Model (BDM) — Personality : Grounded in Big Five and OCM research, mapping work style, decision-making, collaboration and resilience to reveal who a person is Ability Identification Model (AIM)— Ability : A multi-aptitude assessment across reasoning domains, converted into career-weighted strengths to reveal what a person can master. All three assessments are completed online, at the user’s own pace — no exam hall, no added pressure. CareerIPA’s proprietary AI mapping engine then cross-references the DRM, BDM and AIM signals and deliver a ranked, explainable shortlist of careers, each recommendation accompanied by the reasoning behind it — never a generic, black-box list. Certified counsellors and an AI copilot (to assist the counsellors) then help turn that insight into a concrete action plan covering admissions, certifications and next steps. One Platform, Every Stakeholder CareerIPA unifies distinct user journeys on a single platform. 3 – Science-Backed Assessment Models 11 – Stakeholder Types Served 1 – Unified AI + Human Guidance Platform School Students (Class 8–12) Challenge: Stream and course choices shaped by marks, popularity, or peer pressure. How CareerIPA Helps: Personalised, evidence-based recommendations before the choices become expensive. articles.title: Axis Bank partners with SSAIT to set up India's first fully integrated Olympic-standard ...
articles.content: Banking & Finance Axis Bank partners with SSAIT to set up India’s first fully integrated Olympic-standard Archery Centre in rural India Supported by Axis Bank, the project will be developed over a three-year period and will scale SSAIT’s existing archery ecosystem to make it a world-class high-performance centre built to international standards. SMEStreet Edit Desk 22 Aug 2026 14:11 IST Follow Us New Update Listen to this article 0.75x 1x 1.5x 00:00 / 00:00 In a landmark step towards strengthening India’s Olympic sporting ambitions, Axis Bank, one of the largest private sector banks in India, in partnership with the Sanjeeva Singh Archery Institute Trust (SSAIT), today announced the development of the Axis Bank Sanjeeva Singh Olympic Archery Centre in Kanhauli, Eastern Uttar Pradesh. Envisioned as India’s first fully integrated Olympic-standard archery centre in a rural setting, the Centre aims to create a direct pathway from grassroots talent identification to elite international competition by bringing world-class training infrastructure, sports science, residential facilities and education together in one campus. Supported by Axis Bank, the project will be developed over a three-year period and will scale SSAIT’s existing archery ecosystem to make it a world-class high-performance centre built to international standards. The initiative will expand access to top-tier sporting infrastructure beyond metropolitan centres, while creating new pathways for talented athletes from underserved regions. India's archery success story has increasingly emerged from rural and tribal regions, yet access to high-performance training infrastructure remains concentrated in a limited number of locations. Led by Sanjeeva Singh, Olympian and recipient of both the Arjuna and Dronacharya Awards, the Centre seeks to address this gap by establishing a world-class sporting destination in eastern Uttar Pradesh, making advanced coaching, sports science and competition-ready infrastructure accessible to aspiring athletes closer to their homes. Located less than 45 km from Gorakhpur Airport, the Centre is expected to serve as a regional hub for talent identification and advance training across eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, northern Chhattisgarh and north-eastern Madhya Pradesh. The Centre will feature Olympic-standard indoor and outdoor archery ranges, competition-grade infrastructure, advanced simulation capabilities for training under tournament conditions, and sustainable athlete-friendly facilities. Supported by a dedicated control room, climate-controlled training spaces and integrated monitoring systems, the facility is designed to enable year-round training and competition readiness. Integrated with a 100-bed residential wing, it will host training camps, selection trials and competitions, and has been benchmarked against leading archery institutions in South Korea, USA, UK and Switzerland. A key differentiator will be its internationally benchmarked sports-science ecosystem, featuring advanced performance analytics, physiological monitoring, 3D shot analysis and specialised athlete-development tools to support precision training and high-performance outcomes. Speaking on the occasion, Vijay Mulbagal, Group Head - Wholesale Bank Coverage, Corporate Salary, Sustainability & CSR, Axis Bank, said, “Access to world-class infrastructure can transform sporting potential into sporting excellence. Through the Axis Bank Sanjeeva Singh Olympic Archery Centre, we are helping create a first-of-its-kind ecosystem that brings together world-class facilities, sports science, education and residential training within a single campus. articles.title: From South India's First IVF Baby to Thousands of Families: Ramakrishna Hospital ... - ThePrint
articles.content: Subscribe to Notifications ANI Press Releases From South India's First IVF Baby to Thousands of Families: Ramakrishna Hospital Continues to Shape Fertility Care VMPL New Delhi [India], August 22: For many couples, the journey to parenthood isn’t always straightforward. While advances in reproductive medicine have transformed the way infertility is treated, hope still begins with choosing the right team, the right technology, and the right care. What is IVF and when is it recommended? In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) is one of the most advanced Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART), where an egg and sperm are fertilized outside the body in a specialized laboratory. The resulting embryo is then carefully transferred into the uterus to achieve pregnancy. IVF may be recommended for couples experiencing: – Blocked or damaged fallopian tubes – Male infertility, including low sperm count or poor sperm motility – Ovulation disorders such as PCOS – Endometriosis affecting fertility – Unexplained infertility after unsuccessful natural conception – Age-related decline in fertility – Recurrent pregnancy loss requiring advanced fertility evaluation With continuous advancements in reproductive medicine, today, choosing the best IVF hospital in Coimbatore is about more than access to technology. It is about finding a centre with proven clinical expertise, experienced specialists, ethical practices, and compassionate care that supports every step of the fertility journey. At Sri Ramakrishna Hospital, fertility care is built on decades of clinical excellence and innovation. The hospital created a historic milestone in 1991 by delivering South India’s first IVF baby an achievement that marked the beginning of a new era in reproductive medicine across the region. Since then, the fertility centre has continued to evolve, embracing the latest advancements in Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) while maintaining a patient-first approach. Today, the hospital offers comprehensive fertility solutions under one roof, including IVF, ICSI, IUI, fertility preservation, advanced embryology, high-end diagnostic evaluations, and personalized treatment protocols tailored to every couple’s unique needs. Every treatment plan is supported by experienced fertility specialists, skilled embryologists, dedicated nursing teams, and state-of-the-art laboratory infrastructure that adheres to international standards. Over the years, Sri Ramakrishna Hospital has helped more than 20,000 families experience the joy of parenthood, reinforcing its reputation as the best IVF hospital in Coimbatore. With an impressive IVF success rate of up to 80% in suitable cases, the hospital continues to deliver outcomes that reflect its commitment to clinical excellence, evidence-based treatment, and continuous innovation. The hospital’s legacy extends beyond successful pregnancies. With over 50 years of trusted healthcare excellence, patients receive holistic fertility care that combines advanced medical expertise with emotional support throughout their journey. International patients also benefit from dedicated visa assistance, treatment coordination, multilingual support in Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, English, Hindi, and other languages, ensuring a seamless experience from consultation to recovery. The fertility centre continually invests in advanced ART technologies, precision diagnostics, and modern laboratory practices that improve embryo selection, treatment planning, and overall success rates. articles.title: Katra-Banihal rail boost: India's toughest mountain route gets a major speed upgrade
articles.content: Business News LATEST Trends Katra-Banihal rail boost: India’s toughest mountain route gets a major speed upgrade Katra-Banihal rail boost: India’s toughest mountain route gets a major speed upgrade Indian Railways raises the Katra-Banihal section’s maximum speed to 100 kmph, promising faster travel across the 111-km Himalayan route featuring 33 tunnels and iconic bridges. Business Today Desk Aug 22, 2026, Updated Aug 22, 2026 6:00 AM IST Advertisement Subscribe to Notifications 1/6 Speed Boost The Katra-Banihal rail journey is getting faster as Railways raises the maximum permissible speed on the 111-km mountain route to 100 kmph. The upgrade comes after completing all safety checks, reducing travel time across one of India’s most challenging railway corridors. 2/6 Mountain Marvel Cut through some of the toughest Himalayan terrain, the Katra-Banihal section is more than just a railway line. Built across deep valleys, steep slopes and complex geological zones, it represents one of Indian Railways’ most ambitious engineering challenges under the USBRL project. 3/6 Bridge Wonders The route carries engineering landmarks that have captured global attention. From the Chenab Railway Bridge, the world’s highest railway bridge, to the Anji Khad Bridge, India’s first cable-stayed railway bridge, the section showcases extraordinary infrastructure built in extreme conditions. 4/6 Tunnel Network Behind the faster trains lies a massive underground effort. The Katra-Banihal section features 33 tunnels carved through the mountains, allowing trains to navigate the difficult Pir Panjal and lower Himalayan ranges while maintaining safer and smoother connectivity. 5/6 Kashmir Link The speed upgrade strengthens the dream behind the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Railway Link — connecting the Kashmir Valley with the rest of India through an all-weather rail network. The improved service is expected to benefit passengers, tourism and regional economic activity. 6/6 Vande Bharat The route gained national attention after Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off the Katra-Srinagar Vande Bharat Express in June 2025. With the latest speed enhancement, the strategically important railway corridor moves closer to delivering faster and more comfortable journeys. Advertisement

articles.title: Paradip, India's First Piped-Gas Port Township: Why Dharmendra Pradhan Was the Key Architect
articles.content: Odisha Translate Translate Paradip, India’s First Piped-Gas Port Township: Why Dharmendra Pradhan Was the Key Architect| Special Report S Sanjeev Kumar Patro Browse all articles by Sanjeev Kumar Patro · 22 hours ago · 7 min read Man behind Paradip Port's Moment! Key Points Paradip became India’s first major port to provide PNG connectivity to its dedicated residential township. The milestone traces back to the Urja Ganga pipeline, Dhamra LNG Terminal and Paradip gas spur developed during Dharmendra Pradhan’s petroleum tenure. Paradip Port’s ₹20-crore PNG project, backed by its strong financial surplus, has connected 546 residential quarters in Madhuban. Bhubaneswar: When Union Ports, Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal inaugurated the Rs20-crore Piped Natural Gas (PNG) network at Paradip Port on Friday, the port achieved a distinction that older and larger Indian ports had not: its residential township became the first among the country’s 12 major ports to receive piped gas. The milestone at Paradip, however, did not emerge overnight. The final connection of gas pipelines to 546 residential quarters at Madhuban was the last stage of an infrastructure chain that had been built over nearly a decade. At the centre of that chain was a series of decisions taken during the tenure of former Union Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. From pushing the eastern India gas grid to developing a pipeline spur towards Paradip and expanding the City Gas Distribution network, the infrastructure architecture was put in place years before the Paradip Port Authority took the final step of piping gas into its township. The story, therefore, is best understood through a timeline. 2016: The eastern India gas grid gets its push The first major building block came with the Jagdishpur-Haldia-Bokaro-Dhamra Natural Gas Pipeline project, popularly known as the Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga . Under Pradhan’s tenure as Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister, the long-delayed eastern gas pipeline project was pushed as part of the larger effort to expand the natural gas network into the energy-starved eastern states. The objective was to create the basic gas highway that eastern India, including Odisha, had long lacked. Without that trunk pipeline, there could be no city gas network at Paradip and no PNG connection inside the port township. July 2017: Dhamra LNG Terminal foundation laid The second major piece of the energy architecture came on July 8, 2017 , when the foundation stone for the Dhamra LNG Terminal was laid. The terminal was designed to become a major gas entry point for eastern India. Imported LNG could arrive at Dhamra, be converted back into natural gas and then injected into the pipeline grid. Thus, even as the Urja Ganga pipeline was being developed to carry gas across the eastern region, Dhamra was being developed as a major supply source for that network. March-December 2017: The city gas and Paradip connection The next layer was local distribution. As the government expanded the City Gas Distribution framework, Jagatsinghpur district, where Paradip is located, became part of the expanding gas distribution geography....

articles.title: KEO launch to take AI computing to every government school in Karnataka:Shivakumar
articles.content: Pramesh S Jain Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Friday launched KEO,an AI-enabled computing device developed through KEONICS,describing it as a step towards democratising access to artificial intelligence and ensuring that every government-school student in the state gets an opportunity to learn and build with emerging technologies. Shivakumar said the launch was not merely about introducing a new device but about giving shape to a larger vision of making technology and AI accessible to children across Karnataka, from rural villages to urban centres. “We don’t just launch a device.We launch a dream—the dream that every child in Karnataka,from rural villages to city centres,can learn,build and shape the future of artificial intelligence,”he said. The government will initially deploy 1,000 KEO AI PCs in government schools,with the stated objective of eventually taking the technology to every government school in Karnataka,particularly those in rural areas. “This is not a pilot.This is a commitment.This is a promise,” Shivakumar said,stressing that a child’s access to technology and opportunity should not be determined by their geographical location. He said KEO represented the evolution of KEONICS from supporting technology projects to developing solutions aimed at creating wider social impact. The device, he said, could help students learn coding, artificial intelligence,machine learning and electronics while enabling teachers to use AI-based interactive learning tools. ‘Talent must not be limited to Bengaluru’: Shivakumar said KEO would help create a distributed talent pool across Karnataka instead of allowing technology opportunities to remain concentrated in Bengaluru. “For years, talent flowed to Bengaluru.Today,with KEO, we are reversing that narrative,”he said,adding that a rural student using KEO could become a technology innovator, entrepreneur or problem-solver of the future. He described the initiative as an effort to democratise opportunity and bridge the digital divide between government and private schools. “Your child’s ZIP code should never determine their access to technology and opportunity,”he said. The Chief Minister also called upon industry partners and CSR organisations to join the government’s effort to take KEO to every government school. KEONICS’ legacy : Tracing Karnataka’s technology journey,Shivakumar recalled the role of former Chief Minister Devaraja Urs in establishing Electronic City and the subsequent contribution of former Chief Minister S M Krishna in strengthening Karnataka’s technology infrastructure. He said KEONICS had played a crucial role in the development of Electronic City and in Karnataka’s transformation into a global technology hub. “Devaraja Urs and S M Krishna built the foundation for an entire generation of innovation,”he said. Shivakumar said KEO reflected Karnataka’s belief in developing homegrown technology solutions for local needs and demonstrated what could be achieved through collaboration between the government, KEONICS and the semiconductor and technology ecosystem. He said KEO would evolve with technological advances, with more powerful processors,improved AI models and expanding possibilities for students. “KEO is just the beginning,”Shivakumar said,reiterating the government’s objective of ensuring that every government school in Karnataka has access to the device. articles.title: Exicom First In India to Manufacture Liquid-Cooled Power Modules for EV Chargers
articles.content: Home 2 Wheeler News 2 Wheeler News Car News Exicom First In India to Manufacture Liquid-Cooled Power Modules for EV Chargers By Mohit Soni 22/08/2026 Follow Us On: Follow Us On: Exicom Tele-Systems Limited (BSE: 544133 | NSE: EXICOM), one of India’s leading EV charging and Critical Power companies, today announced the start of manufacturing for advanced liquid-cooled AC and DC power modules at its Hyderabad Smart Manufacturing Facility, making it the first company in India to produce this class of liquid-cooled power electronics for global markets. This launch strengthens Exicom’s push to make India a global base for technology-forward manufacturing. It also marks an important step in Exicom’s long-term product roadmap, broadening the canvas for high-value exports and further strengthening the company’s differentiation as a design-led manufacturer. Heat is the quiet enemy of EV charging. Reliability studies attribute nearly 60% of power electronics failures to thermal stress, with every 10°-15°C rise in temperatures doubling components’ failure rate. Liquid cooling technology solves this problem at the source. Liquid coolant absorbs and transfers heat far more effectively and can hold internal temperatures roughly 10°C lower than air-cooled systems. Building on Tritium’s in-house liquid-cooled capability, this technology brings a globally proven high-power charging architecture to Indian manufacturing ahead of the curve. This class of liquid cooled modules have been refined across some of the toughest charging environments in the world and pack more power into a compact footprint, run continuously at high loads and cost less to operate over their lifetime. Moreover, their fully sealed design keeps out dust, moisture and salt air, directly protecting against the everyday conditions that shorten charger life in the field. Initial production of these modules will primarily serve North America and Europe, supporting Tritium’s DC charger portfolio including TRI-FLEX™ ultra-fast DC chargers and DC-FLEX™ charging systems. Subsequent phases will help bring this globally proven charging technology closer to Exicom’s customers including Charge Point Operators, Fleets and OEMs with Tritium’s range of DC fast chargers, which are now being deployed in India. Over time, liquid-cooled architecture will be designed into Exicom’s flagship Harmony DC chargers, opening a new line of high-value power electronics exports from India. Commenting on the development, Anant Nahata, CEO and Managing Director, Exicom, said: “Anyone who has stood next to a fast charger on a 45-degree afternoon knows what heat does to electronics. EV Charging is getting faster with chargers running more hours a day, and customers expect them to work every season and at every site. Globally, liquid cooling has become the architecture of choice for high-power charging. We are bringing this technology to India. Local manufacturing matters because we now own more of that technology ourselves. We can engineer it, improve it and adapt it faster, for our customers here and across the world.” Manufacturing liquid-cooled modules demands precision. Exicom’s recently inaugurated Hyderabad Smart Manufacturing Facility, designed with advanced automation, digital traceability and specialised testing will be the base for manufacturing these modules for domestic and international markets.
